title: Gods, Rich-Men, Angels: Three Discrete Degrees of Divine Emanation
arc: The teaching answers why three names — "gods," "rich-men," "angels" — are spoken in the cosmos for divine beings, and shows that these names mark three discrete degrees of emanation from the Father, each summoned by the call of the one above it and reckoned to a distinct house: the Greatness, the Beloved of Lights, and the Ambassador.
reading:
This chapter is a piece of cosmic onomastics: it asks why human mouths in the cosmos name divine beings by three different titles — "gods," "rich-men," and "angels" — and answers that the three names correspond to three discrete degrees of emanation from the Father. The teaching is not really about vocabulary; it is about the structure of influx. Each name marks a distinct station in the descent of Divine Truth from its inmost source toward the souls in need of redemption.

The first degree is the gods. These are the emanations whom the Father himself summoned, "alone, through himself," and stood upright before the likeness of his Greatness. They are the primal proceeding of love and wisdom from the Divine Esse, set immediately before the inmost. Because they came directly from the Father's own call, they belong to the house of the Greatness — that is, to the celestial degree, the inmost of heaven. They are also the host that "came forth to the contest and brought low the Enmity": Divine Truth in its first emanation is already the power that overcomes opposition to the Lord at the highest level.

The second degree is the rich-men (ⲣ̄ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲟ). The teaching states this carefully: "the rich" is the call of the first gods. That is, where the Father called the gods directly, the gods in turn make the call by which a second order of emanations comes forth. These are described as "the all of the first living word" — the spiritual degree, Divine Wisdom proceeding from Divine Good. Their work is to fulfil "the purpose of heart of the Greatness" in the worlds above and below: they translate the Father's will from the celestial into ordered cosmic operation. They belong to the house of the Beloved of Lights, that is, Divine Love in its emanating aspect, the principle by which all love returns home. The rich are rich because they bear and dispense the substance of the first call into the second degree.

The third degree is the angels. By exactly the same pattern, "angels" is the call of the rich-men: as the gods generated the rich, so the rich generate a third-order embassy. These are sent "in an embassy and an apostolate to the Building" — that is, into the cosmos as construction, the natural creation. They reach down even to all the souls that have been transmuted (passing through metensomatosis in the mingled state) and bring them hope and trust. They belong to the house of the Ambassador "who is of glory" — the Third Ambassador, the awakening call of Divine Truth that reaches captive light. The angels are therefore the operative descent of the prior two degrees into the natural, the missioning by which the celestial and spiritual finally touch souls.

The arc of the whole teaching is thus a single ladder of summonses. The Father calls; that call constitutes the gods. The gods call; that call constitutes the rich. The rich call; that call constitutes the angels. Three discrete degrees — celestial, spiritual, natural — each one the calling-forth of the next, each housed in a distinct cosmological seat: Greatness, Beloved of Lights, Ambassador. The reason the human mouth in the cosmos uses three names is that there really are three orders standing in three houses, and each name preserves the trace of the level from which the being was sent. The teaching closes by pointing out that all who bear each name in any region of heaven are "reckoned to" the corresponding house — the names are not loose honorifics but assignments to discrete states of love and wisdom.

Read in correspondence, the chapter teaches the doctrine of discrete degrees in the heavens: Divine Truth does not descend by continuous gradation but by stations, each generated from the one above by an act of calling, and each preserving in its very name the memory of its descent. The "rich" are rich because they hold what the first call gave them; the angels are angels (messengers) because their being is constituted by the embassy laid upon them. The gods, rich, and angels together are the threefold articulation by which the Father's inmost reaches the soul.
